      "observations": [
        "The entire two-path owned change adds h1 2em, h2 1.5em and body table 1em rules to shared common.css, plus .major-section 1.5em to the support stylesheet. It changes no UIFontSize logic, preference or registration call and adds no test.",
        "Actual stylesheet consumers were checked. about:support loads Thunderbird's aboutSupport.css, and its application-basics h2 carries major-section. The theme manifest overrides the global in-content common URL; all three platform common skins import the shared file. Preferences is one directly checked consumer of that overridden URL. This is not a complete inventory of every about page or proof of all final cascades.",
        "The fixed accepted styles retain these em values. The nearby system-font-size root condition and the selected UIFontSize update paths are distinct inputs: the module sets or clears a registered window root size, and separately has an edited/browser guard for content-body sizing. These selected contracts do not establish that every page is registered or that every font setting controls every browser.",
        "Manual style review treats the em/rem choice as this patch's local sizing outcome, not a repository-wide rule. Selector scope, platform import indirection and page-specific heading override were checked independently of formatter concerns. No changed assertions exist. No font pixels, Linux/macOS/Windows rendering, accessibility result or cure of the whole Troubleshoot Mode report is claimed.",
        "Full current Bug 1832899 and D268311 are retained, including both actual historical inline bodies and the complete timeline. Earlier review objected to oversized about pages and proposed page-specific body sizing/registration. Later discussion separated message-font preferences from registered UI font updates; these are historical explanations, not a complete current setting audit.",
        "The reviewer requested rem for consistency; the author said rem stopped tracking the intended UI size. Final approval followed, while the owned and accepted source uses em. The requested rem spelling was not adopted merely because a reply was marked Done or the revision was approved. No source rule or measured visual result is inferred.",
        "The Bug's Troubleshoot Mode and OS/default-font reports concern broader historical states. This small CSS landing does not by itself prove that every reported font problem was fixed."
